the_rock.name: the Rock
the_rock.what: the asteroid the station was built inside: a metal-rich rubble body hollowed in the L2 yard (2214-2251) to take the habitat cylinder, which turns inside it on its bearings; the Rock does not turn
the_rock.size: about 7.6 km across and 9.4 km long; 200-500 m of rock between the cavity and space
role: quarry: the voyage's store of metals, minerals, water and volatiles
mount: the Drive and the Port are set in its stern and bow
the_rock.mining: the Steward's diggers (tenders' big kin) work its outer face, never the cavity side: cutting, crushing and sorting in vacuum; the spoil is packed back as shield
popular: 'the station is inside a mountain' (half the children believe it)
'the Rock' is also slang for anything you can't change

the_spindle.name: the Spindle
the_spindle.what: the central cylinder on the axis, 200 m across and running cap to cap (8 km); it does not turn with the land; its skin carries the Sunline
inside: the great refineries: vacuum smelting, electrolysis, zone refining
the chip line: one fixed process, the Thirty-Two (see TECH_LIMITS)
cell works: the boards' sealed cells
the tool line: hand tools, bearings, fasteners, motors' laminations
the_spindle.fed_by: the end-cap hubs: ore and ice come in from the Rock through the bow and stern hubs, along the axis, in near-zero gravity
the_spindle.people: no one has been inside since the Second Lockdown (VY 178); before it, Wardens worked the hub galleries in pressure suits
popular: 'the Sunline is the furnaces showing through' (it isn't)

makes_for_people: raw materials at the Drops (see DROPS)
hand tools, fasteners, bearings, blades, wire, pipe fittings: plain, unbranded, the same design for 500 years
the board (pattern HMP-1): an allotment to each of the three vehicle works
a fixed number a year since VY 350
replacement corner pods for the boards: leave a worn pod at a Board Drop, a new one is there within the week
LCD panels, rationed by the Assembly's Panel Board
food stock, cloth, medicines, soap, paper: through the Chutes (the Draw)
aerostats, since the Gift of the Air (VY 405), at the aerodromes

drops._about: Placeholder until the Drops are defined in detail (the user, 2026-10-01: 'we will define those Drops later').
drops.what: designated places throughout the habitat where the Steward's machines deposit raw materials for people: hatches in the floor that open at night, a fenced yard round each; towns grew works and smelters beside them
kinds: scrap metal: offcuts, worn parts, mixed steel and aluminium -- the works' main feed
alloy ingots and billets: steel, aluminium, copper, brass, some nickel and chromium
deposits of minerals people refine themselves: sulfur, iron ore, copper ore, bauxite, phosphate rock, lithium salts, graphite, silica sand, limestone, salt, clay
the Board Drops: the three vehicle works' yards (Harrow Falls, Port Carrow, Solana Point), where the year's boards and exchange pods arrive
the Parts Drops: Thirty-Twos and panels, at the Registry's depots in Kessler and the big towns
drops.versus_chutes: the Chutes hand out finished goods stock (the Draw); the Drops leave materials to be worked
words: 'a Drop night' (the nights a Drop opens; scrappers wait at the fence)
'scrapper' (one who picks a Drop for a living)

processors.name: the Thirty-Two
processors.what: the one processor board the Steward makes for people since the Fourth Lockdown set the Floor (VY 350): a 32-bit chip of early-2000s power (about 400 MHz, 64 MB of memory, a flash store, serial and network ports) on a standard card
processors.supply: plentiful: tens of thousands a year; they never wear out and are reused for generations
processors.know_how: people know how to integrate them -- the College's Book of the Thirty-Two, written from the Wardens' manuals in the Floor's first years and printed for anyone, and the College's courses
processors.the_cap: however many are joined, they never add up to a mind: the Steward makes no other kind, the network's links are slow, and every attempt to gang thousands together has failed or been found and stopped (the Lantern, VY 350, was the last that got far)
popular: 'a Thirty-Two is a Thirty-Two' (all machines are as smart as each other)

dot_matrix.name: dot-matrix displays (monochrome LCD)
dot_matrix.what: the Steward makes thousands of monochrome LCD dot-matrix panels a year (against a few hundred OLEDs and colour TFTs), from a thumbnail line to a bus's destination sign: black on green or grey, backlit green at night. Common, not free: a population heading for 250,000 and more shares them
uses: vehicle dashboards (a readout beside the gauges: range, charge, the trip)

panels.name: panels (OLED and colour TFT screens)
panels.what: OLEDs and high-resolution colour TFTs are the scarce ones: the Steward's panel line makes a few hundred a year; the Assembly's Panel Board rations them
panels.vehicles: passenger vehicles get none: gauges and a monochrome dot-matrix readout. Some heavy vehicles on Steward boards have the board's own small colour status panel, sealed into the deck

gauges.what: every car and van has electromechanical gauges: speed, pack charge, motor temperature, an ammeter; warning lamps; driven from the controller's Thirty-Two
gauges.makers: instrument makers, many of them clock and watch families (Fenwick's are the best known)

radio.name: the Wire set and the Wire slot
radio.what: every car has a radio, but it is its own unit: a Wire set slides into a standard opening in the dashboard (the Wire slot) and plugs into a standard socket (power, aerial, speakers, the dimmer line)
radio.origin: the slot is the old Earth single-DIN size, taken from the Wardens' manuals; made the standard by the Wire Slot Accord (VY 452) when the Wire went on the air
radio.culture: sets are bought, swapped, stolen and handed down; a good set outlives three cars; 'pulling your set' when you park in Solana Point

tech_limits.why: the Floor (the Fourth Lockdown, VY 350). The Third Lockdown (VY 271) had already pulled people's goods back to the late 21st century; when people built the Lantern out of exactly those machines, the Steward judged that a further regression would one day be needed unless it set a level people could live on for the rest of the voyage and never threaten the ship from -- and it would rather set it once, gently, than regress again. The College teaches this; Waymakers say it is keeping them humble; most people never think about it -- the Thirty-Two is simply what a computer is

platforms._about: The boards. Engineering numbers (dimensions, modules, masses, power) in tools/vehicles/platforms.py and godot_project/remake/vehicles/chassis/platforms.json.

pattern.name: the Pattern (the Steward Pattern)
pattern.what: the board's body interface: the deck top 0.50 m above the ground; body mounts every 0.75 m along both side rails; power and control at the pattern socket behind the front axle. Every board, the Steward's or people's, keeps it: any body fits any board of its width
pattern.law: the Standard Pattern Act (VY 398) made it the law for people's boards

boards.name: the Steward board (pattern HMP-1)
used_for: the Long Calm's pods and vans (old stock)
boards.build: one piece per span: a printed lattice of Spindle alloy, bone-like, the sealed cells set in it; four or more corner pods (motor, steering, brake, suspension and controller in one), bolted on; everything by wire
boards.look: sleek and organic, pale and smooth like bone; very little metal; nothing to see but the deck and the pods
sizes: heavy (2.45 m track, up to 4 axles; trams ride on coupled heavy boards)

boards.name: the Harrow Ladder
used_for: the family car of the Northland
boards.build: two boxed rails of rolled-and-welded steel tube with crossmembers; the battery in four steel crates between the rails; one motor in the middle driving the back wheels through a differential and a De Dion tube on leaf springs; drum brakes
boards.look: heavy, square, rivets and welds, red oxide primer and black paint; you can see everything and fix most of it with a welder

boards.name: the Carrow Keel
boards.build: a ship's keel: a big central tube holding the battery as a string of cartridges, loaded from a hatch at the back; a perimeter hoop (the gunwale) and outrigger ribs; a motor at each axle, inboard, with half-shafts; coil springs and wishbones all round
boards.look: rounded, careful, navy and bronze, the keel tube polished; a shipwright's work

boards.name: the Solana Lattice
boards.build: a bicycle maker's space frame: thin chromoly tubes triangulated and brazed into lugs; the battery as side-loading cassettes you can swap in two minutes; motors in the back wheel hubs; light springs
boards.look: airy, all triangles and bright lugs, sun yellow and cream; light and quick, and it shows a crash

steward: diggers on the Rock's outer face cut, crush and sort ore in vacuum; ice and volatiles are baked out
in the Spindle: vacuum and electric smelting, molten-salt electrolysis for aluminium and titanium, zone refining for silicon; slag back to the Rock
powder-bed fusion for fine parts (the boards' lattices, the pods' housings) and wire-arc deposition for big ones; designs topology-optimised: material only where the loads go, so the parts look grown
one fixed chip process (the Thirty-Two) and one small panel line; deliberately never improved
sealed solid cells for the boards; never given out loose
carts through the Undercroft's galleries to the Drops, the Chutes and the Board Drops, at night
people: electric arc and induction furnaces turn Drop scrap into steel and aluminium again; every works and most towns have one
rolling mills make strip and plate (the Falls Rolling Mill at Harrow Falls is the biggest); tube is rolled from strip and seam-welded, or drawn (Solana's chromoly)
arc and gas welding for frames; brazing into lugs for light tube (Solana)
sand casting of aluminium and iron: brackets, hubs, motor housings
lathes and mills, some run by Thirty-Two controllers (the 'smart lathes' of Kessler and Harrow)
induction motors, copper wound by hand and machine in winding shops; ferrite magnets (no rare earths come from the Drops) for small hub motors
LFP cells from Drop iron, phosphate rock, lithium salts and graphite: prismatic cells in steel cans, built into packs, crates and cassettes by hand; heavier than the Steward's and long-lived
tyres from farmed rubber (Russian dandelion and guayule, grown in the Southland), vulcanised with Drop sulfur, filled with carbon black from the waste kilns
float and pressed glass from Drop silica sand at Port Carrow and Marlowe
boards built round the Thirty-Two; hand-wound relays and switches; gauge works
lead-free enamels and red oxide primer; colours are a works' signature

companies.name: Harrow Motor Works
companies.yard: the Falls Yard (the Wardens' Motor Pool No. 2, the Assembly's from VY 274), on the river below the Falls
companies.ethos: build it heavy, build it once; if it breaks, a welder fixes it
companies.buyers: farmers, tradespeople, the Northland and the Kettle Valley; the Marshals' patrol trucks
companies.allotment: the largest share of Steward boards (it builds the farm machines and the haulers)
companies.reputation: loved and mocked: 'a Harrow will outlive you, and you'll feel every bump of it'
companies.now: about 46% of people's boards; the Ladder little changed in a century; president Della Brenneman-Szabo hired 600 of the Mill No. 2 hands in VY 494

companies.name: Carrow Coach Company
companies.yard: the Harbour Yard (the Wardens' Motor Pool No. 1, the Assembly's from VY 274), in the shipyard
companies.ethos: a car is a vessel: build it like a ship, ride like a boat
companies.buyers: Kessler's lawyers and officials, the North Shore, cab firms, undertakers; the better sort
companies.allotment: the road trams and coaches: every tram on the roads rides on Carrow-bodied Steward boards
companies.reputation: respected, a little resented: 'Coach money'; the Keel Recall still hurts
companies.now: about 31% of people's boards; aluminium keels since VY 431; president Lionel Vance-Okafor

companies.name: Solana Cycle & Motor
companies.yard: the South Yard (the Wardens' Motor Pool No. 3, the Assembly's from VY 274), joined to the Ybarra Cycle Works
companies.ethos: light is fast, fast is fun, and you can carry the battery home
companies.buyers: the young, the South Shore, couriers, racers; anyone who wants the cheapest car going
companies.allotment: the smallest share: refuse trucks and the South Shore's farm machines
companies.reputation: the fun one and the fragile one: 'a Solana is a bicycle that got ideas'
companies.now: about 23% of people's boards and rising; the Solana Swap's cassette stations in every South Shore town; president Inés Ybarra-Moreno

rivalries.why: the old feud: work truck against carriage, Kettle Valley against North Shore; the Keel Recall (VY 427), which Harrow's men were accused of gloating over
the Port Carrow - Solana Point rivalry of the Spin Cup carried onto the road; the Ring Run
mostly contempt both ways ('bicycles' / 'tractors'), and an alliance against Carrow in the Allotment Inquiry
